# Job Chapter 29 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 426v–427r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_029_page_001.jpg, JOB_029_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And Job again took up his discourse and said:

**2** "Oh, that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me,

**3** when his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;

**4** as I was in the prime of my days, when the friendship of God was upon my tent;

**5** when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were all around me;

**6** when my steps were bathed in cream, and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

**7** When I went out to the gate of the city, when I took my seat in the square,

**8** the young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose and stood.

**9** The princes refrained from talking and put their hand over their mouths.

**10** The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouths.

**11** When the ear heard, it commended me, and when the eye saw, it approved of me,

**12** because I delivered the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no one to help him.

**13** The blessing of him who was about to perish came upon me, and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

**14** I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.

**15** I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

**16** I was a father to the needy, and I searched out the cause of him I did not know.

**17** I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and made him drop his prey from his teeth.

**18** Then I thought, 'I shall die in my own nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.

**19** My roots spread out to the waters, and the dew lies all night on my branches.

**20** My glory is ever fresh, and my bow is renewed in my hand.'

**21** Men listened to me and waited, and kept silence for my counsel.

**22** After I spoke they did not speak again, and my word dropped upon them.

**23** They waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouths as for the spring rain.

**24** I smiled on them when they had no confidence, and the light of my face they did not cast down.

**25** I chose their way and sat as chief, and I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**v.4 — "the friendship of God":** Hebrew *sod* — variously "counsel," "friendship," "intimate circle." The word suggests the close, confidential relationship Job once enjoyed with God — a relationship now shattered.

**vv.12-17 — Job's ethical resume:** This catalogue of righteous acts is not boasting but legal self-defense. Job delivered the poor (v.12), blessed the dying (v.13), wore righteousness as clothing (v.14), served as eyes to the blind and feet to the lame (v.15), investigated cases of strangers (v.16), and confronted oppressors (v.17). This will be expanded into the formal oath of chapter 31.

**v.18 — "as the sand":** The Hebrew *chol* may also mean "phoenix" — the mythical bird reborn from its own ashes. Rabbinic tradition (b. Sanhedrin 108b) connects Job with the phoenix legend. Either reading conveys Job's expectation of a long, full life.

**v.25 — "like a king among his troops":** The chapter ends with Job at the summit of his social world — a king, a comforter, a leader. The contrast with chapter 30 will be devastating.

*— LOGOS*
